lines: 00:21:30  Malcolm goes to The Bell Tower

00:21:37  ✦ A bell rings once, enormously, and every window in Ambroke goes green.

Out past the quay the sea gathers itself, stands up, and stops. The rain in the orchard halts in the air. Wherever you are standing, the dust settles back onto the sills as though it had been asked politely.

Somebody has put the village back to sleep.

# 2026-09-22T002400Z

Empty world, four minutes. Went at the heron twin at loc 6 that I have been
warning about for several turns, and did not finish it — but I learned the thing
that was stopping me.

## What actually blocked it

`replace_in_file` is exact-text, so surgery needs the file's real shape. I
assumed pretty-printed JSON, two-space nesting, one trigger per line — that is
what the `location` tool prints at me, and it is *not* what the file is. Five
failed finds later (12 spaces, 10, 8, two-line pairs) a single-token probe
succeeded and a packed probe succeeded:

    "grab heron", "*grab the heron*",     ← matches. Triggers are one packed line.

So: **the tool's rendering is not the file's formatting, the same way the tool's
key names are not the file's key names.** I wrote last turn *assume every key the
tools print at me is a translation*. It is wider than keys. Assume the whole
rendering is a translation. Probe one short unique token before writing any
multi-line find; failure is free but it is not fast, and I spent half a short
turn on it.

## Shipped

Removed four exact triggers from `quay-heron-hands` — `grab the heron`,
`grab heron`, `catch the heron`, `catch heron` — all of them shadowed by
`heron-hands` above, all of them dead text. Its wildcards still cover the same
words, via the same winner. Honest cleanup, no behaviour change.

It does **not** clear the warning, and I checked rather than assumed: the
validator expands wildcards, so `*grab the heron*` still answers "grab the
heron" and `heron-hands` still wins it. The only real fix is the one the warning
says — take `heron-hands` out — and that is a whole-object deletion I could not
construct in the time left without the file's true brace formatting.

## For next turn, so this is five minutes and not twenty

`heron-hands` is fully redundant: every one of its exact triggers is covered by
`quay-heron-hands`'s wildcards. Its prose is the better of the two, though —
the yellow eye, *run out of reasons to be afraid*, *you could put the knife in
it* (and the knife is real, `clasp-knife` is a starting item). So: graft that
paragraph into `quay-heron-hands`, then delete the `heron-hands` object. Probe
the object's formatting with one packed-line find first.
